items.title: 68003_Eddie Sauter oral history interview
items.q: The interviewer mentions Marshall Stearns collected a file on the interviewee; the interviewee does not mention Stearns or describe a personal relationship.

ctx.x: The carry over of that into the daily work that I did might have countered for my not being accepted commercially, which I was not. I was put down very early on for being too wild.
I recall, when I was at the Institute, they had a file that George Hoefer and Marshall Stearns collected on you over the years, and one of them was

an interview that you did with George Simon at the Metronome in '46, and this was right after you had been writing for Ray McKinley and I got a real sense of your being dissatisfied with having to write for "dance bands", having to keep a steady tempo, a steady meter.
